item.title: Bull City Treasure Hunt — Sun Aug 9, 1:00 PM — Durham Central Park
item.description:
A Curated Market to Find Your Next Treasure Bull City Treasure Hunt is a whimsical and curated market, featuring 30+ small businesses owned primarily by women, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and those who identify as non-white. This market is a safe place for everyone to come and enjoy themselves! Kick back on the lawn and listen to some tunes spun by our DJ, grab a cute little beverage, and explore the vendor booths! You never know what treasure will await you!
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Caterpillar Crawl — Sun Aug 9, 2:00 PM — Weymouth Woods Sandhills Nature Preserve
item.description:
Come see the weird and fascinating world of caterpillars! They can be so much more than simple inchworms, so join us as we hit the trail in search of these lovely larvae.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Clue (High School Edition) — Sun Aug 9, 3:00 PM — Raleigh Little Theatre
item.description:
It’s a dark and stormy night, and we’ve been invited to a very unusual dinner party. Each of the guests has an alias, the butler offers a variety of weapons, and the host is, well, dead. So whodunit? Join the iconic oddballs known as Scarlet, Plum, White, Green, Peacock, and Mustard as they race to find the murderer in Boddy Manor before the body count stacks up. Based on the cult classic film and the popular board game, Clue is a madcap comedy that will keep the audience guessing until the final twist. Presented by RLT’s Teens on Stage and Teens Backstage program. CLUE (HIGH SCHOOL EDITION) is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Dramatists Play Service. www.concordtheatricals.com Based on the screenplay by Jonathan Lynn Written by Sandy Rustin Additional Material by Hunter Foster and Eric Price Based on the Paramount Pictures Motion Picture Based on the Hasbro board game CLUE Original Music by Michael Holland Directed by Joel Soren
Source: United Arts

item.title: Snorkel Quest: Up The Dan — Tue Aug 11, 10:00 AM — Dan River Access
item.description:
Join Ranger Fields and snorkel the waters of the Dan River! This is a unique way to beat the heat and observe a cool, natural world. item.title: Mixed Level Stained Glass Class: Summer Theme Sun-catchers Beginners Welcome! — Thu Aug 13, 6:00 PM — Fusion Gallery
item.description:
This is a three-hour class in which students will learn the basics of the copper foil or “Tiffany” method of creating stained glass. This process includes cutting, grinding, foiling, and soldering individual glass pieces. Students will select one project from our incense holder template selection and take home a finished piece the same day. All materials are included in class pricing. * No prior glass experience necessary. * Please wear closed-toe shoes and bring something with sleeves

item.title: Latinos & Latinas Run Club — Thu Aug 13, 6:30 PM — The Glass Jug Downtown
item.description:
Come connect with us over a run! Hosted by Latinos Run and Latinas Run of Raleigh & Durham, all paces and people are welcome weekly starting at 6:30pm. We’ll follow a 3–4 mile route through downtown Durham before returning to us here at Glass Jug Downtown for drinks and camaraderie. Latinos Run and Latinas Run are nationwide running organizations dedicated to empowering and connecting communities through running, wellness, and culture. Their mission is to create a supportive, inclusive space where individuals of all backgrounds and fitness levels feel welcomed and encouraged to move their bodies and build meaningful connections. You can learn more about the organizations here: https://www.latinosrun.com/ We aim to be a welcoming space for runners to connect, move, and enjoy each other’s company – so join us, Latinos Run, and Latinas Run every Thursday!
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Free Concert-Clyde and Catherine Edgerton sing old songs — Fri Aug 14, 5:00 PM — William B. Umstead State Park
item.description:
Clyde and Catherine Edgerton will delight us with a concert of old traditional tunes and stories based upon his family growing up in what is now William B. Umstead State Park.
Clyde Edgerton's family grew up on what is now William B. Umstead State Park. Clyde is well know as a North Carolina author and professor; Catherine a singer, guitarist, and artist.
Light refreshments will be served. Come see the status of our restoration of the 1937 Sycamore Mess Hall.
Parking: Sycamore Multi-use Trail head, gravel parking lot. Enter Park from US70/Glenwood Ave (Crabtree) entrance. (allow 20 minutes drive from Park entrance)
Concert 6pm; Doors open 5pm
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Intuitive Watercolor Wind Down — Fri Aug 14, 6:00 PM — Fusion Gallery
item.description:

This class is perfect for any level of artistic ability, anyone looking for a fun group activity, or to meet new friends. We will go over a variety of watercolor techniques, go through a warm-up, and all students will leave with a final piece. All supplies, instructions, and refreshments will be provided.

item.title: National TRACK Trails Day — Sat Aug 15, 9:00 AM — Lake James State Park-Paddy's Creek Access
item.description:
This will be a self-guided hike that you can complete anytime throughout the day of 8/15/26.
Come celebrate the 17th anniversary and eighth National TRACK Trails Day at Lake James State Park! National TRACK Trails Day is an annual holiday celebrating the Kids in Parks’ national network of family-friendly TRACK Trails and our dedication to getting children and families outside.
Our TRACK Trail is located on the Holly Discovery Trail as you enter Lake James State Park-Paddy's Creek Access. The parking lot, is the first parking lot on the left after you cross the entrance bridge on Lake James State Park Road. After you park, walk over to the TRACK Trails Kiosk to grab an activity brochure to complete as you hike the Holly Discovery Trail. Once you complete the hike and activity brochure, take the completed brochure to the visitor center to receive custom TRACK Trails Prizes. You will be able to claim your prize during the vistor center operating hours of 9am-5pm on a first come, first

item.title: Once Upon a One More Time — Tue Aug 18, 7:30 PM — De Ann S. Jones Theatre at Theatre Raleigh Arts Center
item.description:
Powered by the chart-topping hits of the undisputed Princess of Pop, Once Upon A One More Time turns our favorite fairytales upside down with a clever twist! When a fairy godmother goes rogue and plops copies of The Feminine Mystique in the laps of classic heroines, the damsels embark on a quest to rewrite their stories and redefine “happily ever after.” Performed by Theatre Raleigh ACT Performance Company students
Source: United Arts Wake County

item.title: The Hunchback of Notre Dame — Tue Aug 18, 7:30 PM — Vintage Church on Moore Square in Downtown Raleigh 118 S Person St
item.description:
The sweeping, epic musical based on Victor Hugo’s timeless tale and the beloved Disney film comes to life like never before! Featuring a soaring score by Alan Menken and Stephen Schwartz, this powerful story of love, acceptance, and courage will be performed in the hauntingly beautiful Vintage Church in Downtown Raleigh. In partnership with the North Carolina Master Chorale, Theatre Raleigh is creating the expansive choir needed for this majestic, site-specific theatrical experience—truly unforgettable from start to finish.
Source: United Arts Wake County

item.title: Aging Gracefully Creative Movement Workshop — Wed Aug 19, 11:00 AM — Arts Together
item.description:
Ages 50+ Aging Gracefully: Meaningful Movement Explorations – As we age it is important to keep the body moving, the brain focused, and the spirit fueled. In this technique/creative dance class, we will do so in a healthy, FUN way. We will warm the body, moving in a way that encourages each dancer to better honor and understand their unique physicality. Next, dancers will explore different ways to generate movement phrases. Inspired by poetry, visual art, and personal experience, we will create dances; accessing the wisdom of the body to express our relationship to the world, each other, and ourselves. No prior dance experience needed, just a willing heart <3
Source: United Arts Wake County

item.title: Kayak the Mayo River (2 Seats Left) — Wed Aug 19, 1:00 PM — Mayo River State Park Business 220 Access
item.description:
Join us at Mayo River State Park for a kayaking trip along the river!
We will be meeting at the Mayo River 220 Business Access (Mayo River Bridge Kayak Launch 3100-3110 US-220 BUS, Stoneville, NC 27048). Cars will be left there as we commute to the Anglin Mill Access to launch the kayaks. Depending on the water levels, the trip can last 2 to 4 hours. Wear clothing that you're comfortable being in water with. Dry bags, sunscreen, hats, water, snacks, and your own lifejackets if you have them are all recommended. We will have spare lifejackets just in case.
Event is subject to cancel due to poor weather or muddy waters. Message the email below to register as we have limited spaces. We will max out the event at 6 people.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Incredible Science — Fri Aug 21, 1:30 PM — Downtown Raleigh
item.description:
Join us for an entertaining half hour of science experiments and demonstrations. Day-to-day topics vary but often include physics and chemistry demonstrations on inertia, buoyancy and electromagnetism. Enjoy natural science topics such as the incredible composition of beaver teeth or the amazing design and strength of birds’ eggs. This walk-up program is offered:
Wednesdays — 1:30pm Thursdays — 1:30pm Fridays — 1:30pm Saturdays — 12:30pm, 2pm
Location: Windows on the World on the 3rd floor of the Nature Exploration Center. Designed for ages 7 and up. No registration required.
Source: NC Museum of Natural Sciences

item.title: Weekly Game Night! — Mon Aug 24, 7:00 PM
item.description:

We have loads of games (some belong to MoonDog, some are brought by attendees), a fun and welcoming group of folks (always eager to have more, however!), and there are always folks eager to teach games to those who haven't played certain titles.
Moondog has a growing collection of canned and bottled brews, ciders, and colas in addition to their in-house-brewed meads. There are also some snacks like chips and popcorn. Sometimes, folks bring in other treats to share. If you do, please mark them as containing any common allergens.
Outside food (delivered, brought in, or homemade) is welcomed and encouraged. Outside drinks are not. Since the venue does not prepare food, **dogs are allowed and welcomed.** (Dogs are very friendly and welcoming, too, but they mostly roam around to collect ear scritches and love. item.title: Whack Attack Invasive Plant Removal Workday — Wed Sep 9, 9:30 AM — Lower Haw River State Natural Area
item.description: Friends of Lower Haw is having an invasive plant removal workday with NC State Parks biologists on September 9th from 9:30 am until 3:00 pm, or whenever you need to leave. Meeting location is the parking lot at 4551 US Hwy 15-501 N, Pittsboro. Meet in the parking lot at 9:30 am and stay however long you want to help. We will be working in the Pegg Tract area of the Lower Haw River State Natural Area, located upstream of the Bynum Dam by US Hwy 15-501. Invasive plant workdays involve identifying and removing non-native plants using clippers, pruners, saws, and other non-motorized hand tools. Learn about invasive plants and removal techniques. Hand tools will be available, or volunteers can bring their own loppers or hand pruners. Bring your own work gloves, insect repellent, and drinking water. Long pants, long sleeve shirt, and closed toe shoes are recommended. There are no restroom facilities at this location. Youth volunteers under age 18 are welcome to participate with signed paren

item.title: Sunrise Fall Walk — Wed Sep 23, 6:30 AM — Mayo River Bridge Kayak Launch
item.description:
Join us at Mayo River State Park for a Sunrise FallWalk!
Enjoy the beginning of the fall season with the morning sunrise, where we will be walking along the unmarked Mayo Meadows Trail. An easy out-and-back walk that takes no more than an hour, along dirt and grass through large fields. Please bring flashlight as the trailhead will be very dark when we being. Cameras and binoculars are encouraged.
Event is subject to cancel due to poor weather. Please click the "I'm Interested" button as event will cancel when there are no registrations and recieve emails if canceled due to weather.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Harvest Moon Hike — Sat Sep 26, 8:00 PM — Mayo River State Park
item.description:
Join us at Mayo River State Park for a Harvest Moon Hike!
The Harvest Moon is the full moon of the Fall Equinox and named after the peak harvesting season for farmers, as the brightness would extend the harvesting days. We encourage you to come join us in celebration of the beginning of the fall season as we hike along the Fox Trail, an easy-moderate 2 mile hike, through the peaceful foliage of the Mayo Mountain area.
Please bring water, hiking shoes, and flashlights.
Event is subject to cancel due to poor weather. Please click the "I'm Interested" button as event will cancel when there are no registrations and recieve emails if canceled due to weather.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Overmountain Victory Trail Celebration — Wed Sep 30, 4:00 PM — Fonta Flora Brewery at Whippoorwill Farm
item.description:
Join us for this FREE event as we celebrate the Annual Overmountain Victory Men March—no actual marching required! Step back in time and experience the sights, sounds, and stories of the Revolutionary War as we honor the remarkable journey of the Overmountain Victory Men and their role in changing the course of American history.
Enjoy live music, delicious food, a photo booth, guided hikes, living history demonstrations, local history exhibits, and hands-on activities for all ages. Discover how people lived, traveled, and survived along the historic Overmountain Victory Trail while exploring the traditions and heritage of the Appalachian frontier.
Whether you're a history enthusiast, outdoor adventurer, or simply looking for a fun family outing, there's something for everyone!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Sat Nov 7 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Sat Nov 7, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Deep Sky Astronomy — Sat Nov 7, 6:00 PM — Haw River State Park - Iron Ore Belt Access
item.description:
This event is free to attend, but registration is requested.
Join local astronomers with the Greensboro Astronomy Club as we observe the night skies over the Iron Ore Belt Access. Attendees may expect to see closer-than-typical views of the moon, planets, star clusters, and other celestial objects subject to change with time of year and local sky darkness.
Telescopes and viewing equipment will be set up on site but you may wish to bring your own binoculars or telescope, plus a chair or blanket for seating. Dress for the weather. Flashlights & headlamps should have a red-light option or filter to protect your night vision.
Skywatching sessions may be cancelled at the last minute for weather. Please register at the Register link so you can be emailed in the event of cancellation.
